guides.definition: Creates a three.js scene, camera, renderer, and visible mesh. Browser/editor content: import three.js in the target page or bundle and serve it over HTTP; the Web APIs surface is editor-only.

parameters.name: fieldOfView
parameters.description: Vertical camera field of view in degrees.

examples.title: Create a blue cube scene
examples.explanation: The light makes the standard material visible and the initial render paints a frame immediately; dispose GPU resources when removing long-lived scenes.

guides.definition: Uses renderer.setAnimationLoop to update a mesh and render every frame. Browser/editor content: import three.js in the target page or bundle and serve it over HTTP; the Web APIs surface is editor-only.

parameters.name: axis
parameters.description: Rotation axis x, y, or z.

examples.title: Rotate the created mesh
examples.explanation: setAnimationLoop integrates with regular displays and immersive sessions; the time argument is in milliseconds.

guides.definition: Updates the projection matrix and renderer size when the viewport changes. Browser/editor content: import three.js in the target page or bundle and serve it over HTTP; the Web APIs surface is editor-only.

examples.title: Follow the browser viewport
examples.explanation: Changing aspect alone is insufficient; updateProjectionMatrix applies the new camera projection before the next render.
